newsitem.title: FRANCE: French economists panel sees 1.8 pct growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: French economists panel sees 1.8 pct growth in 97.

text.p: French economic growth is expected to reach 1.8 percent this year, below the government's official forecast of 2.3 percent, a panel grouping economists from banks and industry said on Wednesday.

The forecast, by the French Assocation of Company Treasurers (Afede), is slightly below a consensus forecast of bank economists who expect growth of around two percent or more after 1.3 percent last year.
Afede said it did not believe trade would contribute much to growth since any increase in exports would be offset by a rise in imports due to the economic recovery.
It also said consumer spending was expected to rise by just 1.6 percent after an estimated increase of 2.5 percent in 1996, while much of the recovery in growth would be due to adjustments to stocks.

"No element of final demand (excluding stocks) is on the horizon for the time being which has the potential for enough acceleration to be able to pull up the rest of activity and spark a real recovery," Afede said in a statement,
It forecast the total public deficit would be reduced to 3.2 percent of gross domestic product this year, rather than the three percent forecast by the government.
"The Maastricht target on public deficits will only be reached through cosmetic measures," it said.
France must reduce its deficit to three percent of GDP this year to comply with Maastricht treaty goals on entry to European economic and monetary union.

In December, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development forecast France's public deficit at 3.2 percent of GDP this year, but said this could be reduced to three percent through additional measures.
